architecture_question: Did the widened architecture-v2 policy/value heads materially improve value quality and playing strength over the architecture-v1 Mini lineage?
comparison_limits: The architecture-v1 value audit used a different checkpoint and probe dataset, so its 0.4239 validation MSE is context rather than a controlled head-width comparison.
Architecture-v1 matched candidates used 1,000- and 5,000-game datasets; the first fresh architecture-v2 lineage used 100 games, so the run does not isolate head width as the sole causal variable.

The training datasets were generated with different self-play search contracts: architecture-v1 used 64 simulations, exploration 0.7, and progressive widening 3.0/0.5, while architecture-v2 used 100 simulations, exploration sqrt(2), and progressive widening 1.5/0.5. Evaluation search was matched, but this training-data mismatch confounds any attribution to head width.

decision.conclusion: The widened heads did not materially improve the realized architecture-v2 lineage. Held-out value error was high, value guidance weakened matched-MCTS play relative to policy-only guidance, and every v2 guidance mode lost all 40 games to the unchanged heuristic baseline.

next_apparent_bottleneck.name: bootstrap self-play learning-signal quality and coverage, especially value-target generalization
next_apparent_bottleneck.evidence: Fresh random-bootstrap self-play supplied only 100 games, 331 validation positions from nine held-out games, and no validation draws; the widened value head reached 0.1655 training MSE but 0.8039 validation MSE, while adding value guidance changed matched-MCTS play from 13-8-19 to 4-4-32.
next_apparent_bottleneck.next_experiment: Improve or enlarge bootstrap teacher/search data under a frozen comparison contract, and require held-out value diagnostics plus paired strength gates before attributing gains to head capacity.
